clue.text: Vegetables straight from the pan: a hit, of course

parts.note: chips are fried potatoes, loosely counted as vegetables
food straight from the pan is hot

explanation.surface: A cook describes freshly fried vegetables served up at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' means on a golf course: a chip shot is a short lofted stroke onto the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf stroke is a hit made on the course, and the chip is one such stroke.

clue.text: Hard to demand a change with no machine involved

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of the words are to change into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to ask for change from a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' makes ANDMADE from DEMAND plus A, placed after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crafted by hand rather than by machinery has no machine involved in its making.

clue.text: Computer expert in favour of language rules, say

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, so in favour of

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: grammar is the body of rules of a language

explanation.surface: A computer specialist supports strict rules for writing language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' turns GRAMMAR into the sound-alike ending GRAMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes software is an expert at computers, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Suffering from mood swings in all sorts of places?

definitions.meaning: going between high spirits and low spirits, as with mood swings
the idiom for searching everywhere, top to bottom

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both alternating highs and lows of mood and the idiom for searching everywhere.

clue.text: About to board smart English warship

indicators.note: to board is to get on, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: trim means neat and smart
re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to embark on a smart English naval vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars, used as a warship.

clue.text: Name, one adopted by girl

indicators.note: taken in by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl takes in a child and gives it a name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's first name, so an example of a name.

clue.text: Wind is up, low murmur initially

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word murmur

explanation.surface: The wind is rising and a low murmur begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns IS into SI. 'Low' is the cattle noise, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A simoom is a hot, dry, dust-laden desert wind of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Any number of coins is enough to create anxiety

parts.note: N stands for any number in mathematics
euros are European coins
taken as written

explanation.surface: Worrying about whether one has enough coins causes anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by persistent anxiety, so the general condition stands for it.

clue.text: Offer further help, giving answer to daughter immersed in work for exam

indicators.note: immersed in means sunk inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to revise is to study for an exam

explanation.surface: A parent helps a daughter who is buried in exam revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Immersed in' puts AD inside REVISE, splitting it RE-VISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise again is to give further counsel, which is offering more help.

clue.text: Number, one way and another, is doing well

indicators.note: the clue word is read two ways, one of them backwards

parts.note: a number is a song in a show
a number is a song in a show

explanation.surface: A performer's number, whichever way it goes, is going down well.
explanation.walkthrough: The one clue word 'Number' does duty twice, once as its abbreviation turned round and once as a song in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone performing in top form, so it means doing well.

clue.text: Bad lad breaking into shelter is given punishment

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a harbour is a shelter, for ships or for people

indicators.note: bad here means spoilt, so the letters are put in a corrupted order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A delinquent who breaks into a shelter is sentenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like a description of the lad, but it is the signal to scramble him.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal servitude with heavy physical toil was a punishment imposed by the courts.

clue.text: Regular portions of lean meat for monk

indicators.note: regular portions means every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A monk eats measured helpings of lean meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher.

clue.text: Accuses individuals using corrupt means repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the rearranged word is written twice
corrupt means spoilt, so the letters are put in a corrupted order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone levels accusations by using underhand methods again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means identifying particular people as guilty, so publicly accusing individuals.

clue.text: Joint runner's-up medal given to team

parts.note: the runner-up wins the silver medal
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A runner-up shares a silver medal with the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective (shared) but is a noun: silverside is a cut of beef, the outer part of the topside.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a cut of beef from the hindquarter, a joint for roasting or salting.

clue.text: Informed about royal valet finally being promoted

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: advised means informed or notified
ER is the cipher of the reigning queen, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word valet

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a royal valet has at last been given a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote a product is to publicise it, so promoted and publicised are synonyms.

clue.text: Show pleasure, covering each unit of distance

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to smile is to show pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone grins at every stage of a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical mile is a measure of distance at sea, so it is a unit of distance.

clue.text: Tabloid covering carefully-selected matches leading to a eugenic triumph

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a perm is a permutation of football matches picked on the football pools coupon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid reports a pools win that leads to a triumph in breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game on match results; a perm is a chosen combination of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nietzschean superior human being is what eugenics aimed to breed, its ideal triumph.

clue.text: Gets confused right away about the French exams

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
away means gone, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: ravels means becomes tangled or confused
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone gets muddled straight away over their French examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'immediately' but means remove the R; AVELS is what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A levels are English school-leaving examinations taken at about eighteen.

clue.text: Meal one finished early after mad uncle Henry entered

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the next
entered means went inside, so one piece goes within the other
mad means crazed, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: finished early means the word is stopped before its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A meal ends early after a deranged uncle called Henry walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' makes LUNCE, which H enters to give LUNCHE; 'after' sets that before the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: A luncheon is a formal word for lunch, a midday meal.

clue.text: With it, chump served up chicory

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a chump is a fool

explanation.surface: A trendy fool serves up a dish of chicory.
explanation.definitionFit: Witloof is a variety of chicory grown for its blanched leaves, also called Belgian endive.

clue.text: Old film star's teeth such a perfect colour?

definitions.meaning: the American actress of silent serials such as The Perils of Pauline
perfect teeth are likened to the lustrous shade of pearls

explanation.definitionFit: Pearl White starred in silent film serials, and the phrase also names a lustrous whitish shade.

clue.text: Appoint, for token

definitions.meaning: to appoint someone is to allocate them to a task
read as two words, meaning by way of a token or signal

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to allot or appoint, and split in two it means by way of a token.

clue.text: Race against time for this little piggy

parts.note: a run is a race

explanation.surface: The nursery rhyme pig races against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest animal in a litter, so a little piggy.

clue.text: See poplars metamorphose into tropical trees

indicators.note: metamorphose means change form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener watches poplars magically transform into tropical trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose apple is a tropical tree of the myrtle family grown for its scented fruit.

clue.text: Love dipping into favourite author

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A reader dips lovingly into the work of a favourite writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet is a writer of verse, and so an author.

clue.text: One part of Oxford just like all the others?

definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a laced shoe, and this is the arched middle part of the foot or shoe
two words meaning in conformity, marching in time with everyone else

explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched part of a shoe such as an Oxford, and split it means in conformity.

clue.text: American coin one flipped

parts.note: the angel was an old English gold coin

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American coin is tossed once.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a resident of Los Angeles, so a kind of American.

clue.text: Perhaps trying to catch out an author

definitions.meaning: in cricket, fielders try to catch the batsman out
Henry ..., the eighteenth-century English novelist of Tom Jones

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the fielding side tries to catch batsmen out, and Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones.
